 TAL Education: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

 Learn more On its second-quarter fiscal year 2027 earnings call, held on Oct. 29, 2026, TAL Education (NYSE:TAL) announced net revenue rose 15% year over year to $995 million. Higher efficiency in core offline tutoring offset severe industry contraction in home learning hardware. 
 Three takeaways from the call explain how management is navigating these shifting market dynamics. 
 1. Hardware Industry Contractions Drag Down Overall Growth 
 Shrinking market demand and higher chip costs pressed the learning device segment. This dynamic created a headwind for top-line expansion while offline tutoring programs maintained steady enrollment. 
 The industry as a whole for learning devices has contracted, as noted by several independent third-party market reports, and these conditions have affected our performance.
-- Alex Peng, President and Chief Financial Officer 
 2. Operational Discipline Drives Significant Operating Margin Expansion 
 Cost controls and operational leverage helped non-GAAP income from operations, which excludes stock-based compensation expenses, double year over year to $248 million. Operating margin reached 24.9% as efficiency gains across corporate departments offset rising device costs. 
 The continued improvement in our operating margin reflects operating leverage, efficiency gains, and disciplined resource allocation.
-- Alex Peng, President and Chief Financial Officer 
 3. Shareholder Returns Evolve With Special Dividends and Repurchases 
 Management shifted toward systematic capital returns by pairing ongoing share repurchases with a special dividend. The $55.2 million dividend payout reflects underlying cash generation despite fair-value declines in the investment portfolio. 
 Looking ahead, we intend to make shareholder returns a more systematic part of our capital allocation approach using both dividends and share repurchases.
-- Jackson Ding, Deputy Chief Financial Officer 
 Looking Ahead 
 Revenue growth is moderating across scaled business lines, but physical classrooms keep retaining students. Management relies on offline scale and proprietary software to stabilize market share while keeping expenditure constrained. 
 We will continue to bring together our experience in education and our capabilities in technology to improve the learning experience.
-- Alex Peng, President and Chief Financial Officer 
 Hardware remains a strategic entry point for independent home study. Management balances ongoing software development against current market headwinds to prevent significant full-year losses in devices. 
 Story Continues We want to continue developing this business with a long-term perspective while making sure that our near-term decisions reflect the market conditions we're facing today.
-- Alex Peng, President and Chief Financial Officer
